facts.text: Director Boon Collins' film was loosely inspired by the 1984 Montana abduction of biathlete Kari Swenson by survivalists Don Nichols and his son Dan, who wanted her as a 'mountain bride'.
The poster tagline: 'When she went for her morning jog she didn't realize she'd be running for her life!'
The real victim, Kari Swenson, was a bronze medalist on the 1984 US relay team at the first Women's Biathlon World Championships in Chamonix, France, before her kidnapping that summer.
In the real case, Don Nichols got 85 years and son Dan got 10. Kari Swenson survived being shot, became a veterinarian, and later advised on the 1987 NBC TV movie with Tracy Pollan.
The film's working title was 'Stone Sheep', a nod to the bighorn-style animals that Dan Haggerty's character, Joe Evans, obsesses over. It was renamed Abducted.
In the real case, the shot that hit Kari Swenson collapsed a lung, but she survived, partly thanks to the breathing capacity of a trained endurance athlete.
Kari Swenson, the biathlete who inspired this film, resented media coverage that painted her kidnappers as romantic 'mountain men' instead of criminals.
Writer-director Boon Collins cast Dan Haggerty, TV's Grizzly Adams, right after Haggerty's 1984 cocaine bust. Collins called him a 'piece of work' on the 2024 Blu-ray.
Cinematographer Robert McLachlan, who shot this wilderness thriller on a tiny crew, later filmed Game of Thrones and Ray Donovan. Director Boon Collins says the shoot paid very little.
The whole movie was shot in about 17 days north of Vancouver on a budget under CA$200,000.
Writer-director Boon Collins co-wrote the script with Lindsey Bourne, who also co-wrote the 1995 sequel Abducted II: The Reunion.
Roberta Weiss' river-log struggle wasn't shot in a river. It was a North Vancouver hotel pool lined with weighted black tarp, with the crew splashing her to fake the current.
Roberta Weiss (Renee) was cast in Toronto because director Boon Collins felt she had a 'serious' demeanor. She later played Flame Beaufort on the soap Santa Barbara.
Film distributor Films We Like says Abducted was shot on Mount Seymour in British Columbia, just north of Vancouver.
Lawrence King-Phillips (Vern) was a friend of director Boon Collins' sister from their Ryerson University days. He later lived briefly with Collins and his wife.
Roberta Weiss (Renee) also appeared in the Stephen King adaptation The Dead Zone (1983) and the anthology series Tales from the Darkside.
Dan Haggerty broke his leg just before filming and wore a thigh-high cast. For his close-ups he was rolled along on a dolly, faking his walk.
In long shots, Dan Haggerty's walking was done by Norm Mackie, a lookalike the crew found working at a nearby log sort yard. He took time off work and went uncredited.
Abducted earned a Genie Award nomination for Best Overall Sound at the 8th Genie Awards in 1987, for Peter Clements, David Appleby and Don White.
Dan Haggerty's beard famously caught fire in 1977 when a restaurant patron carried a flaming cocktail too close.
Stephen E. Miller, who plays the Guide, also appeared in the first Rambo film, First Blood (1982).
VideoHound's Golden Movie Retriever called Abducted 'weird and unbelievably tedious', but praised its spectacular wilderness footage.
After its one-week Canadian run, Abducted got wide video distribution worldwide in the late 1980s, including a US release from Prism and releases in Europe, South America and Japan.
Reviewing the 2024 Blu-ray, Brian Orndorf called it 'a bizarrely inert study of relationships and nature'. He said director Boon Collins lacked the imagination for active horror.
In the UK, Abducted came out on VHS from RCA Columbia Home Entertainment.
Kari Swenson returned to competition after her ordeal and finished fourth at a 1986 biathlon event in Oslo, Norway, before retiring.
Director Boon Collins first made his name writing the 1981 slasher Butcher, Baker, Nightmare Maker. He later made a sequel to this film, Abducted II: The Reunion.
The sequel Abducted II: The Reunion brought back Dan Haggerty and Lawrence King-Phillips and added horror regular Debbie Rochon. It later aired on USA Network's late-night USA Up All Night.
A train engineer who was a huge Grizzly Adams fan backed his train up for a second take on the trestle, on one condition: he got to meet Dan Haggerty. Haggerty gave him a signed 8x10.
Director Boon Collins recalls Lawrence King-Phillips (Vern) as a 'tortured soul'. After the shoot he lived briefly with Collins, then returned to Toronto and later died of a heroin overdose.
Abducted opened in Canadian theaters on December 12, 1986, and played for just one week.
